digital_arrest.name: Digital Arrest Scam
digital_arrest.reason_template: Threatens you with arrest or investigation and demands you stay on a call or transfer money.
advice: Hang up or stop replying immediately.
Real police and courts NEVER demand money transfers or 'digital arrests' over WhatsApp or video calls.
Do not transfer money to any 'safe account' - safe accounts do not exist.
Tell a trusted family member or call 101 (non-emergency police) to verify.

fake_kyc.name: Fake KYC / Account Suspension Scam
fake_kyc.reason_template: Creates fake urgency claiming your account or SIM will be blocked unless you click a link.
advice: Do not click the link.
Do not enter any personal details or passwords.
Real banks give plenty of notice by post and do not threaten instant suspension via chat.
Check your account directly through your bank's official app or the phone number on your bank card.

upi_payment.name: UPI / Payment Scam
upi_payment.reason_template: Asks you to enter or share a PIN/UPI to receive money or a refund.
advice: NEVER enter your PIN to receive money - entering your PIN only SENDS money.
Never scan a QR code to 'receive' funds.
Do not share your PIN with anyone, including bank staff or customer service.
Cancel any pending payment requests immediately.

otp_theft.name: OTP / Verification Code Theft
otp_theft.reason_template: Asks you to share a security code or OTP that was sent to your phone.
advice: Never share an OTP or security code with ANYONE.
Legitimate organisations and banks will never ask you for an OTP over the phone or message.
An OTP allows someone to steal your account or authorise money transfers.

fake_delivery.name: Fake Delivery / Parcel Fee Scam
fake_delivery.reason_template: Claims a parcel cannot be delivered until you pay a small fee via an unfamiliar link.
advice: Do not click the link or enter your bank card details.
Scammers use small £1 or £2 fees to steal your full card numbers.
Check the official tracking website directly (e.g., royalmail.com or evri.com) using your original tracking number.

remote_access.name: Remote Access Scam
remote_access.reason_template: Instructs you to install screen-sharing software or grant remote control of your phone/computer.
advice: Do not install AnyDesk, TeamViewer, QuickSupport or any screen-sharing tool.
Disconnect your internet or turn off your device immediately if already connected.
No genuine bank or police will ask to control your phone or screen.

family_impersonation.name: Family Emergency / 'Hi Mum' Scam
family_impersonation.reason_template: Claims to be your son, daughter, or grandchild who lost their phone and desperately needs money.
advice: Do NOT send any money or pay bills to the new account.
Call your family member directly on their OLD, known phone number or speak to them in person.
Ask a personal question only your real family member would know.

fake_bank_hmrc.name: Fake Bank or Government/HMRC Scam
fake_bank_hmrc.reason_template: Impersonates HMRC, tax authorities, or your bank's fraud department to demand payments.
advice: HMRC and real banks NEVER threaten arrest or demand immediate bank transfers over chat.
HMRC never sends tax refunds via WhatsApp with clickable payment links.
Call your bank using the phone number printed on the back of your bank card.

investment_crypto.name: Guaranteed Profit / Crypto Scam
investment_crypto.reason_template: Promises guaranteed or risk-free investment returns.
advice: High returns with 'no risk' are always a scam.
Never send money or crypto to strangers online.
Legitimate financial advisers never promise guaranteed profits.

lottery_prize.name: Lottery / Prize Scam
keywords: pay processing fee to release prize
lottery_prize.reason_template: Claims you won a lottery or giveaway you never entered, asking for an upfront fee.
advice: You cannot win a lottery you never bought a ticket for.
Legitimate prizes never ask you to pay an upfront fee to claim winnings.
Do not send money or bank details.
